review_type: Automated agent visual inspection of cached source frames and alpha tracks; no human acceptance and no annotated ground truth
review_scope: Six discrete pilot frames. No additional inference was run. This review does not establish temporal stability between the samples.

identity_association.status: No discernible identity swap in the six observed frames
identity_association.basis: Striped standing performer maps to P01, bald patterned shirt to P02, gray shirt/profile to P03, dark shirt/cup/stove performer to P04, cap to P05 in both views. Screenplay names remain unverified.

edge_findings: The learned alpha generally follows visible head, torso and arm silhouettes. It is a coarse person mask, not a precision face, finger or object matte.
P03 foreground silhouette remains associated with the same performer after the change from view B to view A, including the visible head and upper body.
P05 cap is included in the silhouette and the outstretched arm is broadly retained in the sampled view B frames.
At 92.2 seconds P04 raises a drinking vessel to the mouth. The mask follows the combined hand and mouth region; it does not provide an independently controllable glass or sip mask.
Fine hair, eyeglasses, fingers, gaps at arm/body boundaries and contact edges require closer review before selective transformation. The masks are 640 by 360 while the source is 1280 by 720.
occlusion_findings: View A includes major foreground occlusion of P02 by P03 and P04 by the seated group. The visible-person masks should be interpreted as partial silhouettes, not complete bodies behind those occluders.
Table, chair, cup and hand contacts are not separately labeled. Overlap ordering and edge contamination must be checked at the exact frames used for a composited effect.
The six samples do not establish that overlapped person alphas are disjoint.
cut_findings: At the view change near 88.2333 seconds, performer masks relocate to the appropriate positions in view A in the sampled post-cut frame 2648.
At 95.0 seconds, the masks are in the appropriate view B positions in frame 2850. No old-view silhouette is discernible in that sampled frame.

Continuous person identity still depends on the authored layout association. A detection centroid crossing a field boundary can misassign identity even when the segmentation silhouette is otherwise plausible.
Mask association and any temporal effect history should reset on a source shot cut; this discrete review is not evidence that all transition frames are artifact-free.
acceptance_status: Useful pilot silhouette trial; pending full moving-footage inspection and artist approval. Detection coverage is not an accuracy score.
